summary: The note reflects on how schools in a local district, post-September 2023, are moving from monocultural, siloed classrooms toward global citizenship and multicultural awareness. It describes initiatives such as the "Windows and Mirrors" program, a Kenya sister-school partnership, technology-based collaboration, expanded language offerings, and curriculum integration of global issues. It concludes that these changes are reshaping student identity and that attention must turn to assessing impact and supporting educators.
one_line: Local district schools adopt global citizenship initiatives, including exchange programs, new languages, and global-issues curricula, shifting students' identity and perspective.
key_facts: Jennifer Holt, a local history teacher, incorporates international perspectives; her students hold video conferences with peers across continents and join international project collaborations.
Holt says teaching is "no longer about memorizing dates and names" but about understanding the interconnectedness of world events.
The district launched the "Windows and Mirrors" program in late October 2023, using literature and media that reflect students' own experiences (mirrors) and introduce outside ones (windows).
Martin Chu, program director of "Windows and Mirrors," wants students to see themselves as capable and significant participants in the world.
On November 12, 2023, Thomas Jefferson High School announced a partnership with a sister school in Kenya, spearheaded by Vice Principal Emily Garcia.
Students in the Kenya exchange can visit the sister school, engage in community projects, and develop language skills in a real-world context.
A 'Code Across Continents' event in September connected students from five countries to develop an app tackling environmental sustainability.
By the start of the 2023-2024 academic year, Mandarin, Arabic, and Portuguese were added to the district's traditional Spanish and French offerings.
Rajeev Singh helped build the Mandarin program at Oakwood High School and says learning a language also teaches culture, people, and history.
Social studies coordinator Lara Kim says students need to confront global issues like climate change, world hunger, and international politics and consider their roles in them.
Technology and digital platforms are used for cross-border collaboration and for developing digital literacy for the 21st-century workforce.
The note says next steps are assessing the impact of initiatives, supporting educators, and sustainably integrating global citizenship into academic life.
